title: Rule proxies that contradict their own rule
body:
From cc's lane:

- `test-highlander-shared-setup` and `real-code-over-mocks` fire on the pattern their own Good prescribes.
- `no-silent-failures` is single-line and never matches its own multi-line Bad.
- `no-parse-ls` claims only SC2012 and misses SC2045, SC2011 and SC2010.
- Every swift and lua rule is undeclared (`critic.rs:855-872`).
- The gate lints the library's own Bad examples, so `strong-assertions/bad_test.exs` cannot be committed without `--no-verify`.

Line numbers as at the audit.

Found by hv's estate-wide doc audit of 2026-09-11 (the audit's orders are in `intent/history/20260911-doc-audit.md`), where it is described as built. Carried in `intent/wip.md` as an unruled defect until 2026-09-13, when that file was leaned and every open defect became an issue. Not worked until hv rules it; a ruled one gets a lane.



**CLOSED 2026-09-14 21:05Z (ic, on vc's batch order).** Fixed in the commit carrying this note, all five findings.
- test-highlander-shared-setup no longer greps for the fixture's definition, which matched its own Good form. Only a count of definitions tells one home from two, and a single grep cannot count. Its hard-coded-email line stays, and it matches the Bad. real-code-over-mocks declares that no greppable proxy is authoritative: a line match cannot tell an internal stub from an external mock, and its old proxy matched the Good and missed the Bad.
- no-silent-failures matches the catch-all clause on its own line (`^[[:space:]]+_ -> (:ok|nil)$`), which its multi-line Bad form writes and its Good form does not.
- no-parse-ls claims SC2012, SC2045, SC2011 and SC2010, so the headless run reports each signal its Detection lists.
- Every swift and lua rule declares that no greppable proxy is authoritative, naming its critic subagent, so none is undeclared.
- The gate no longer lints a rule library's own examples. A STAGED file under the library the run loaded is skipped and named in the report's `skipped_library`, in text and JSON. A file named with `--files` is still read, because that is an ask. Proved by `a_staged_rule_example_is_skipped_and_named_while_a_named_one_is_read`.
